# Knock — welfare navigation, with a human in control

A Next.js / TypeScript prototype implementing the architecture in `mdfile.md`. Cline is used both to build the app and, with credentials, as the runtime conversation agent. Eligibility screening is deterministic TypeScript, not model-generated decisions.

## Run locally

Requires Node 22+.

```sh
cd /home/capsicle/clinehack
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local
npm run dev
```

Open localhost port 3000. With no `CLINE_API_KEY`, the app is an explicitly labeled demo: fill in the profile form, then send a message to run screening. Demo mode does **not** extract facts from free-form messages. With a Cline API key in `.env.local`, restart the server for live extraction and multilingual conversation. `CLINE_MODEL` is configurable; provider availability and billing depend on your account.

## Efficient development pipeline

```sh
npm run validate:data  # required fields, rules, sources and verification freshness
npm test              # deterministic boundary cases and API validation/demo tests
npm run typecheck
npm run build
# all of the above:
npm run check
```

Independent UI and rules/data work use a shared contract in `lib/contracts.ts`. The backend connects those contracts to five restricted Cline tools: `update_profile`, `get_missing_fields`, `match_schemes`, `get_scheme_details`, and `missing_docs_help`. No shell or filesystem tools are exposed to the runtime agent. Result cards are always recomputed from the rules engine, never parsed from model prose.

## Architecture

- `app/page.tsx`: responsive multilingual conversation, profile editor, result cards, voice and read-aloud, auto-location, account chip and profile strip.
- `app/api/chat/route.ts`: bounded JSON requests, schema validation, same-origin checks, concurrency limit and no-store responses.
- `app/api/auth/*` + `app/api/profile`: sign-up/sign-in/sign-out/session and profile sync. Sessions are random 256-bit tokens in httpOnly cookies; passwords are scrypt-hashed; per-process throttling; same-origin and bounded bodies on every route.
- `app/api/applications` + `app/api/account` + `app/api/auth/password`: per-account scheme tracking (Saved/Applied, validated against the catalog), display-name update, and password change with re-authentication — a password change signs out all other sessions.
- `lib/db.ts`: account database on Node's built-in SQLite (`node:sqlite`, zero external services). Stores accounts (email + scrypt hash + name) and each account's profile + language. Conversation text is never stored. Data lives in the gitignored `.data/` directory.
- `app/api/location/route.ts`: bounded reverse-geocoding/IP proxy for auto-location (validated coordinates, timeouts, no logging of coordinates or IPs).
- `lib/chat.ts`: fresh, request-scoped Cline agent, five domain tools, timeout and clearly separated demo path. Live replies are normalised to clean plain text (`lib/text.ts`) for the chat bubble and read-aloud — no markdown, headings or emoji — and the prompt forbids echoing profile details or duplicating the scheme cards.
- `lib/eligibility.ts`: deterministic rule evaluation, unknown-field tracking, ranking and explanations.
- `lib/i18n.ts`: typed, data-driven UI strings. English is the complete base; the other seven languages fall back to English for any missing key. Add a language by adding one code and one dictionary.
- `lib/tts.ts`: enhanced browser text-to-speech — async voice loading, best-voice selection per locale, rate control, play/stop. Provider-agnostic seam so a cloud TTS can be added later.
- `lib/location.ts`: geolocation → state/district with IP and offline nearest-state fallbacks; the user always confirms before it is applied.
- `lib/storage.ts`: only non-personal device preferences (language, voice, speed) in `localStorage`. Profiles sync to your account server-side — no JSON files, no manual export/import.
- `data/schemes.json`: curated catalog of 31 central and state schemes — national scholarships (NSP), PM YASASVI, INSPIRE, state scholarship portals (UP, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra), NSAP pensions, plus farmer, worker, health and housing schemes. Official links only, required documents and application guidance.
- `public/sw.js` + `app/manifest.ts`: offline app shell and PWA installability (maskable icon, shortcuts).
- `tests/`: reproducible rule, request and feature tests.

## Trust, privacy and limitations

- This is a **prototype**, not a government service or official eligibility determination. The catalog now covers 31 central and state schemes, but it is still far from exhaustive — many states have their own portals, and new schemes launch each year. All current rules have partial coverage; exclusions, household checks and official determinations are not fully modeled.
- `last_verified: null` means the scheme has not completed a full policy audit. Official source links are supplied for verification. Ranking is modeled-rule completeness, **not** an approval probability.
- Accounts store email, a scrypt password hash, your display name and the profile/language you save — in a local SQLite file (`.data/`, gitignored). **Conversation text and chat history are never stored on the server.** Matching requests carry the profile and a bounded history only. Live mode still sends conversation/profile data to the configured Cline provider. Do not enter identity numbers, bank details, OTPs or document images.
- Browser speech recognition is feature-detected, requires browser support/permission and may send audio to a browser vendor. Text entry remains available. Read-aloud uses an enhanced browser TTS layer (`lib/tts.ts`) with best-voice selection and rate control, but voice quality still depends on the voices installed on the device; some languages may fall back to a default voice (a hint is shown). Scheme descriptions and rule explanations are currently English.
- Auto-location uses the browser Geolocation API, then a reverse-geocoding/IP proxy (`app/api/location`). Precise coordinates are sent only to that same-origin proxy and are never stored or logged. IP-based lookup is approximate and the result is always shown for you to confirm or edit. If you decline, state/district can be entered manually.
- Your profile, language and preferences auto-sync to your account whenever you are signed in — there are no save buttons and no JSON export/import. "Explore without an account" keeps everything in the current session only. Non-personal voice preferences also cache in this browser's `localStorage`.
- A web manifest and offline service worker are included (`public/sw.js`), which precache the app shell and never cache `/api/` responses (those can contain personal data). This is a best-effort offline shell, not full offline functionality, and a complete installability audit is still recommended before release.
- Live LLM behavior requires credentials and must be manually acceptance-tested. The automated suite does not make paid model calls.
- Before public deployment: add authentication, distributed rate limiting and spend controls, privacy/consent review, policy-data review, provider retention review, deployment-origin configuration and dependency remediation. Current concurrency control is per process, not distributed protection.
- Dependency audit during implementation reported transitive SDK-chain advisories. Do not treat this build as production security-approved; run `npm audit` and review upstream fixes before deployment. No blind overrides were applied.

## Analysis of bugs and requirements

### 1. Voice & microphone bugs

After careful analysis, the real issues I can identify and fix:

**Text-to-Speech (`lib/tts.ts` + `speak()` in page.tsx):**
- **Chrome's long-utterance pause bug**: `speechSynthesis` silently pauses after ~15 seconds on long text and never fires `onend`. This makes read-aloud "stop working" on longer replies → `speaking` gets stuck. Fix: chunk text into sentence-sized utterances spoken sequentially, and/or a keep-alive resume timer. I'll implement chunking + sequential playback with proper `onDone` on the final chunk.
- **Global `speaking` state**: All read buttons show the same "stop reading" state and you can't switch which message is read. Fix: track which message is currently being read (by index) so each button reflects its own state and clicking a different message reads that message.
- **`speak()` toggle bug**: can't switch messages. Fixed by tracking the active message index.
- **`utterance.onend`/`onerror` race with `cancel()`**: when starting new speech, the previous utterance's onend fires calling old onDone. With per-message tracking and a token, this is handled.

**Speech recognition / microphone (`microphone()` in page.tsx):**
- **Error handling bug**: `onerror` shows "Microphone unavailable" for ALL errors including `no-speech` (user just didn't talk) and `aborted` (intentional stop). This is wrong and confusing. Fix: read `e.error` and show appropriate messages; don't show scary error for `no-speech`/`aborted`.
- **`continuous=false` + interim accumulation**: works for single utterance but I'll improve to use `isFinal` properly and support continuous dictation, restarting on `onend` while still listening (auto-restart) OR just keep single-shot but robust. Actually, to keep it simple and reliable, I'll implement proper final/interim handling and auto-restart for continuous dictation until the user stops — this makes dictation actually usable. Hmm, but auto-restart can cause loops. Let me keep it simpler: `continuous` dictation with proper handling of `isFinal` to accumulate final segments and show interim separately. Set `continuous = true` and accumulate finalized results into a stable base.

Let me redesign the mic:
- Maintain a `baseText` (text before dictation started).
- Maintain `finalized` (accumulated final transcripts).
- On `onresult`: compute interim = join of non-final results; compute newFinal = join of final results in this event appended to `finalized`. Actually SpeechRecognition gives cumulative `e.results` where index0..n are all results, each marked isFinal. So the robust approach: on each event, rebuild `finalized` from `e.results` filtering `isFinal`, and `interim` from non-final. Then `setText(baseText + finalized + interim)`.
- On `onend`: if the user didn't manually stop and we want continuous, restart. But to avoid complexity/bugs, I'll restart only if `listening` is still true (i.e., user hasn't clicked stop). Track a `manuallyStopped` ref.

```js
const rec = new Constructor();
rec.lang = locale;
rec.continuous = true;
rec.interimResults = true;
let finalTranscript = '';
rec.onresult = (e) => {
  let interim = '';
  for (let i = e.resultIndex; i < e.results.length; i++) {
    const r = e.results[i];
    if (r.isFinal) finalTranscript += r[0].transcript;
    else interim += r[0].transcript;

  setText(base + finalTranscript + interim);
};
```

So the flow becomes: sign up → create account (unverified) → send verification email → require verification before sign-in (or before full access).

```ts
function hashToken(token: string): string {
  return createHash('sha256').update(token).digest('hex');
}

export function createEmailVerification(userId: number, purpose: EmailPurpose = 'verify_email', ttlMinutes = 60 * 24): string {
  const db = getDb();
  // Invalidate any previous unused tokens for this user/purpose.
  db.prepare('DELETE FROM email_verifications WHERE user_id = ? AND purpose = ?').run(userId, purpose);
  const token = randomBytes(32).toString('hex');
  const expires = new Date(Date.now() + ttlMinutes * 60_000).toISOString();
  db.prepare('INSERT INTO email_verifications (token_hash, user_id, purpose, expires_at, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)')
    .run(hashToken(token), userId, purpose, expires, new Date().toISOString());
  return token;
}

export function consumeEmailVerification(rawToken: string, purpose: EmailPurpose = 'verify_email'): { userId: number } | null {
  const db = getDb();
  const row = db.prepare('SELECT token_hash, user_id, purpose, expires_at FROM email_verifications WHERE token_hash = ? AND purpose = ?')
    .get(hashToken(rawToken), purpose) as { user_id: number; expires_at: string } | undefined;
  if (!row) return null;
  if (new Date(row.expires_at).getTime() < Date.now()) {
    db.prepare('DELETE FROM email_verifications WHERE token_hash = ?').run(hashToken(rawToken));
    return null;
  }
  db.prepare('DELETE FROM email_verifications WHERE token_hash = ?').run(hashToken(rawToken)); // single use
  db.prepare('UPDATE users SET email_verified_at = ? WHERE id = ?').run(new Date().toISOString(), row.user_id);
  return { userId: row.user_id };
}

export function markEmailVerified(userId: number): void { ... } // maybe not needed

export function isEmailVerified(userId: number): boolean {
  const row = getDb().prepare('SELECT email_verified_at FROM users WHERE id = ?').get(userId) as { email_verified_at: string | null } | undefined;
  return Boolean(row?.email_verified_at);
}
```

```ts
export function createTTS(): TTSController {
  const supported = typeof window !== 'undefined' && 'speechSynthesis' in window;
  let preferred: string | null = null;
  let rate = 1;
  let currentToken = 0;

  const stop = () => {
    currentToken++;
    if (supported) window.speechSynthesis.cancel();
  };

  const speak = (text: string, language: Language, onDone?: () => void) => {
    if (!supported || !text.trim()) { onDone?.(); return; }
    window.speechSynthesis.cancel();
    const token = ++currentToken;
    const locale = speechLocale(language);
    const chunks = chunkText(text);
    let index = 0;

    const speakNext = (voices: VoiceLike[]) => {
      if (token !== currentToken) return; // cancelled
      if (index >= chunks.length) { onDone?.(); return; }
      const utterance = new SpeechSynthesisUtterance(chunks[index++]);
      utterance.lang = locale;
      utterance.rate = rate;
      utterance.pitch = 1;
      const voice = pickVoice(voices, locale, preferred);
      if (voice) {
        const native = window.speechSynthesis.getVoices().find(v => v.name === voice.name);
        if (native) utterance.voice = native;
      }
      utterance.onend = () => {
        if (token !== currentToken) return;
        // Chrome can stall on long text; nudge it along.
        window.speechSynthesis.resume();
        speakNext(voices);
      };
      utterance.onerror = () => {
        if (token !== currentToken) return;
        // Skip the failed chunk and continue; if none left, finish.
        speakNext(voices);
      };
      window.speechSynthesis.speak(utterance);
    };

    const cached = window.speechSynthesis.getVoices();
    if (cached.length) speakNext(cached);
    else void loadVoices().then(speakNext);
  };

  return {
    supported,
    speak,
    stop,
    setRate: (r) => { rate = Math.min(1.6, Math.max(0.6, r)); },
    setPreferredVoice: (name) => { preferred = name; },
  };
}
```

Wait, there's a subtle issue with `onerror` continuing to next chunk — if the whole thing errors repeatedly it could loop fast, but each chunk only errors once and index advances, so it terminates. Good. And `onDone` fires when all chunks done. But if a chunk errors and we `speakNext`, we skip it. Fine.

Also add a keep-alive: Chrome pauses after ~15s of a single utterance. By chunking into small pieces (each < 15s), each utterance finishes and triggers onend → next. This avoids the stall. Additionally the `resume()` in onend helps. Good.

```ts
export function chunkText(text: string, maxLen = 180): string[] {
  const sentences = text.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().match(/[^.!?।]+[.!?।]*\s*/g) ?? [text];
  const chunks: string[] = [];
  let current = '';
  for (const sentence of sentences) {
    const s = sentence.trim();
    if (!s) continue;
    if ((current + ' ' + s).trim().length > maxLen) {
      if (current.trim()) chunks.push(current.trim());
      // Hard-split very long sentences.
      if (s.length > maxLen) {
        for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i += maxLen) chunks.push(s.slice(i, i + maxLen).trim());
        current = '';
      } else current = s;
    } else {
      current = (current + ' ' + s).trim();
    }
  }
  if (current.trim()) chunks.push(current.trim());
  return chunks.length ? chunks : [text];
}
```

```ts
    for (let i = start; i < e.results.length; i++) {
```

```ts
async function submitAuth(mode: 'signin' | 'signup') {

    const payload = mode === 'signup' ? { name: authName, email: authEmail, password: authPassword } : { email: authEmail, password: authPassword };
    const res = await fetch(endpoint, {...});
    const data: unknown = await res.json().catch(() => null);
    const obj = data && typeof data === 'object' ? data as Record<string, unknown> : {};
    const message = typeof obj.error === 'string' ? obj.error : null;
    if (mode === 'signup') {
      // register returns 200 with verification_required
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(message ?? t.authError);
      setPendingEmail(authEmail.trim().toLowerCase());
      setDevVerifyLink(typeof obj.devLink === 'string' ? obj.devLink : null);
      setAuthView('verify');
      setAuthPassword('');
```

## Plan

**1. Voice & microphone bugs (fix):**
- **TTS (`lib/tts.ts`)**: Chrome silently pauses `speechSynthesis` after ~15s on long text and never fires `onend`, so read-aloud dies mid-message and `speaking` gets stuck. Fix: split text into sentence-sized chunks and speak sequentially with a cancel-token, plus `resume()` nudge.
- **Read-aloud UI**: a single global `speaking` flag makes every "Read" button show "Stop" and blocks switching messages. Fix: track the active message id.
- **Mic (`microphone()` in `page.tsx`)**: `onresult` rewrites text from a stale `prefix` and mishandles final/interim results; `onerror` shows "Microphone unavailable" even for benign `no-speech`/`aborted`; `continuous=false` cuts dictation short; raw `.stop()` in `send`/`reset`/cleanup leaves the ref in a bad state. Fix: rebuild transcript idempotently from `isFinal`, continuous dictation with guarded auto-restart, accurate per-error messaging, and a single `stopListening()`.

**3. Professional frontend:**
- Redesign the auth screen into a split hero + polished form (password show/hide, strength meter, inline validation), add a "Check your email" verification screen, and refine global styling.

## Summary

I audited and fixed the voice/microphone bugs, rebuilt the login/signup flow with email verification, and gave the frontend a professional polish. Everything is verified: **103 tests pass, typecheck clean, production build succeeds**, and I confirmed the full flow live over HTTP (register → gated login → verify → successful login).

### 1. Voice & microphone bugs — fixed
- **TTS stalled on long replies** (`lib/tts.ts`): Chrome silently pauses `speechSynthesis` after ~15s and never fires `onend`, so read-aloud died mid-message and the UI got stuck on "Stop". Added `chunkText()` to split text into sentence-sized pieces played sequentially, with a cancel-token (ignores stale callbacks), a `resume()` keep-alive, and skip-and-continue on chunk errors.
- **Read-aloud UI** (`app/page.tsx`): replaced the single global `speaking` flag with `speakingId`, so each message's button reflects its own state and you can switch which message is read.
- **Microphone** (`microphone()`): transcripts are now rebuilt idempotently from `isFinal` (no more duplicated/stale text), dictation is continuous with guarded auto-restart through pauses, benign `no-speech`/`aborted` no longer show a scary error, and `not-allowed` gets an accurate "mic blocked" message. Added a single `stopListening()` used by send/reset/sign-out/cleanup so the recognition ref can't leak or auto-restart.

### 2. Login/signup + email verification — added
- **DB** (`lib/db.ts`): `email_verified_at` column + `email_verifications` table (hashed, single-use, expiring tokens) with an idempotent migration for existing databases.
- **Register** creates an unverified account and sends a verification link; **login is gated** until the address is confirmed (403 `needsVerification`).
- New **`/api/auth/verify`** (POST + GET), **`/api/auth/resend`** (generic response → no account enumeration), and a **`/verify`** landing page for the email link. Tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and are single-use.
- **Honest email seam** (`lib/email.ts`): no SMTP is configured, so delivery is logged (redacted recipient) and a `devLink` is returned **only outside production** — the UI labels this clearly. Wire a real provider there to make delivery real.

### 3. Professional frontend
- Redesigned the auth screen into a **split hero + form layout** with password show/hide, a **password-strength meter**, inline email validation, and disabled/loading states.
- Added a polished **"Check your email"** verification screen (with dev-link button, resend, and back-to-sign-in), plus a dedicated `/verify` success/error page.
- Cohesive styling (`app/globals.css`) with responsive breakpoints.

### Notes & assumptions
- **Email is simulated** (no mail provider in this prototype). Outside production you get a clickable `devLink`; in production the link is logged server-side and `devLink` is `null` for security. This is stated in the UI to stay honest.
- I updated `tests/features.test.ts` to the new gated flow and **added coverage** for verify/single-use tokens, login gating, resend enumeration-safety, and `chunkText`. All pass.
- Run `npm run check` as the final gate — it's green.

```ts
/** Classify a Web Speech API error code (SpeechRecognitionErrorEvent.error). */
export function classifySpeechError(code: string | undefined | null): MicErrorKind {
  switch (code) {
    case undefined: case null: case '': return 'unknown';
    case 'no-speech': return 'no-speech';
    case 'aborted': return 'aborted';
    case 'not-allowed': case 'service-not-allowed': return 'blocked';

    case 'network': return 'network';
    case 'language-not-supported': return 'language';
    case 'bad-grammar': return 'unknown';
    default: return 'unknown';
  }
}

/** Classify a getUserMedia DOMException name during the mic pre-flight. */

    case 'NotReadableError': case 'TrackStartError': return 'in-use';

  }
}
```

```ts
}
```

31 | ## Architecture
32 | 
33 | - `app/page.tsx`: responsive multilingual conversation, profile editor, result cards, voice and read-aloud, auto-location, account chip and profile strip.
34 | - `app/api/chat/route.ts`: bounded JSON requests, schema validation, same-origin checks, concurrency limit and no-store responses.
35 | - `app/api/auth/*` + `app/api/profile`: sign-up/sign-in/sign-out/session and profile sync. Sessions are random 256-bit tokens in httpOnly cookies; passwords are scrypt-hashed; per-process throttling; same-origin and bounded bodies on every route.
36 | - `app/api/applications` + `app/api/account` + `app/api/auth/password`: per-account scheme tracking (Saved/Applied, validated against the catalog), display-name update, and password change with re-authentication — a password change signs out all other sessions.
37 | - `lib/db.ts`: account database on Node's built-in SQLite (`node:sqlite`, zero external services). Stores accounts (email + scrypt hash + name) and each account's profile + language. Conversation text is never stored. Data lives in the gitignored `.data/` directory.
38 | - `app/api/location/route.ts`: bounded reverse-geocoding/IP proxy for auto-location (validated coordinates, timeouts, no logging of coordinates or IPs).
39 | - `lib/chat.ts`: fresh, request-scoped Cline agent, five domain tools, timeout and clearly separated demo path. Live replies are normalised to clean plain text (`lib/text.ts`) for the chat bubble and read-aloud — no markdown, headings or emoji — and the prompt forbids echoing profile details or duplicating the scheme cards.
40 | - `lib/eligibility.ts`: deterministic rule evaluation, unknown-field tracking, ranking and explanations.
41 | - `lib/i18n.ts`: typed, data-driven UI strings. English is the complete base; the other seven languages fall back to English for any missing key. Add a language by adding one code and one dictionary.
42 | - `lib/tts.ts`: enhanced browser text-to-speech — async voice loading, best-voice selection per locale, rate control, play/stop. Provider-agnostic seam so a cloud TTS can be added later.
43 | - `lib/location.ts`: geolocation → state/district with IP and offline nearest-state fallbacks; the user always confirms before it is applied.
44 | - `lib/storage.ts`: only non-personal device preferences (language, voice, speed) in `localStorage`. Profiles sync to your account server-side — no JSON files, no manual export/import.

Done. The microphone and voice (read-aloud) features are fully removed, and the app is green.

## What I removed

**UI (`app/page.tsx`):**
- The microphone/dictation button and "listening" indicator in the chat composer
- The "Read aloud" button on assistant messages
- The "Enhanced voice" panel (voice picker + speed slider)

**Code & logic:**
- All speech-recognition code (dictation, pre-flight, error handling) and TTS/read-aloud code (state, refs, effects, `speak`/`microphone`/`stopListening`/`requestMic`/`micErrorText` functions)
- The `speechLocale`/voice-selection wiring and the `window.speechSynthesis` cleanup
- Deleted **`lib/tts.ts`** and **`lib/speech.ts`** entirely

**Tests (`tests/features.test.ts`):** removed the 3 voice/mic tests (voice selection, TTS chunking, mic error classification).

**Strings & docs:** removed 72 now-dead voice/mic entries from `lib/i18n.ts`, and updated `README.md` so it no longer describes the voice/read-aloud feature (architecture list, trust notes, and demo-flow step 4).

## What's untouched & still working
- Text-based chat composer (type + send), profile editor, result cards, scheme tracking
- The full auth + **email verification** flow (register → verify → login), account settings, auto-location
- All 8 languages, PWA/offline shell

## Verification
`npm run check` passes end-to-end:
- **101 tests pass / 0 fail** ✓ · `typecheck` clean ✓ · `build` compiles + prerenders all 17 pages ✓
- Live smoke test: `/`, `/verify`, `/api/auth/session` all return **200**, and a scan of the served HTML shows **zero** voice/mic markers (feature is gone from the rendered UI).

## One minor note
A few now-unused CSS rules for the old voice classes (`.mic-button`, `.read-button`, `.voice-controls`) remain in the minified `globals.css`. They never render (no elements use those classes) and are harmless. I left them untouched because editing the 20 KB compressed stylesheet risks breaking all styling for zero user-visible benefit. I can strip them if you'd like — just say the word.

The app is now a clean, text-based welfare-navigation tool with the auth + email-verification flow and professional frontend intact.
